notes: The eleventh product page (AGL-2769). Same 8-section skeleton as the other detail pages, cloned from `Product — CRM` (1638:8653) so the section rhythm matches. Three things differ from the older decks and are deliberate. (1) `explore` carries TEN cards — every product except the page's own; the older decks record seven because they were extracted when the roster was smaller, and on the 3-up 451px grid ten wraps 3+3+3+1. (2) Nothing on the page states a product count: the `9 products built in` stat the older decks reproduce was stale at ten products and an eleventh falsifies it outright. (3) Both mockups show a Job openings dataset. An earlier draft used products, which implied a Commerce relationship that does not exist — Commerce keeps its own product storage and does not use datasets. Job openings are structured, filterable, shareable across brand sites, imported from a spreadsheet and written by integrations, and no plugin owns them. Every claim was checked against `libs/plugins/data`, `dataset-models.ts`, `dataset-query.ts`, `expand-repeatables.ts`, `plan-entitlements.ts`, the console dataset route and the /v1 handlers in `apps/console/utils/api-v1-resources.ts`; `claimsToVerify` records what was questioned and how each was resolved. The page must not go live before AGL-3105, AGL-3111 and AGL-3113 ship: the hero body, capabilities card 5, the deep-dive and how-it-works step 03 keep copy that only those builds make true, and `claimsToVerify` names the build behind each claim.

sections.heading: Typed datasets, shared across your sites.
body: Datasets are typed collections that belong to your organization, not to a single site. Model the fields once, edit records in the console, bind them to a component that repeats — and let forms, workflows and the API write to the same rows.

image.describe: Datasets records mockup, 920×580, floating card with the standard two-shadow hero treatment. Topbar: Aglyn mark, 'Datasets', breadcrumb '/ Job openings'. Three quota tiles — 'Datasets · this org' 12 / 'of 15 on Pro'; 'Records · Job openings' 48 / 'of 10,000'; 'Dataset storage' 1.4 GB / 'of 5 GB' — the three metered dimensions at Pro's real bands (`datasetsPerOrg` 15, `recordsPerDataset` 10,000, `dataStorageMbPerOrg` 5,120). Below, a records table in the model's display order — Code, Title, Team, Headcount, Status, Posted — with six rows: REQ-118 Senior Brand Designer · Design · 1 · Open · Jul 24; REQ-117 Staff Software Engineer · Engineering · 2 · Open · Jul 24; REQ-116 Data Analyst · Operations · 1 · On hold · Jul 23; REQ-115 Support Specialist · Support · 3 · Open · Jul 23; REQ-114 Content Writer · Growth · 1 · Open · Jul 22; REQ-113 Technical Recruiter · People · 1 · On hold · Jul 22. Status renders as the house chip, green Open and amber On hold.

sections.notes: Two columns: text column left, mockup bleeding off the right edge — the deliberate container-overflow exception the skeleton records. The quota tiles are the point of the shot: they show the product is org-scoped and metered without a line of prose having to say so. The record count stays under 100 because a repeat renders at most 100 records (`REPEAT_MAX_RECORDS`), so the sample never depicts a dataset larger than one repeat can show.

sections.heading: A dataset is not a spreadsheet bolted onto a page. It is a typed model — every field carries a type and its rules, and the console and the API validate each record against it.
sections.notes: Single 34px Bold pull-quote at text/muted, one run, no emphasized phrase. It names the console and the API only, because those are the writers that run `validateDocument`: the console dataset route and `createRecord`/`updateRecord` in `api-v1-resources.ts`. A bound form and a workflow action write through `buildDatasetRecordValues`, which keeps known field ids and drops the rest but checks no type or rule, so 'every write' would be false. The workflow action is the `datasetAppend`/`updateDataset` step: today it runs only as an Actions step, and AGL-3105 makes every server-side Actions step, these two included, a step of a workflow, which is what makes 'a workflow action' exact.

sections.heading: Model it once. Use it everywhere.

items.title: Typed fields, not free text
items.body: Text, boolean, integer, number, date and time, coordinates, list and reference — each with its own rules, checked on every console and API write.

items.title: Rename the label, keep the id
items.body: A field’s display name can change whenever you like; the reference id that bindings, forms and imports use never moves. Descriptions show as hints.

items.title: Shared with the sites you pick
items.body: Datasets belong to the organization, so a collection can drive pages on any site it is shared with, and the server enforces that sharing.

items.title: References and many-to-many
items.body: Point a field at another dataset’s records, allow multiple for many-to-many, or create a join collection that pairs two. A delete checks what still points at it.

items.title: Forms, workflows and the API
items.body: A bound form, a workflow action and the /v1 API write the same rows as the record editor — by id, so renaming a dataset never breaks a binding.

items.title: CSV and JSON, both directions
items.body: Export streams the whole collection and refuses a short file. Import matches columns by id or display name and validates every row on the way in.

sections.notes: Centered eyebrow + heading, 3-column card grid, 2 rows, house icon tiles. Card 1 lists the EIGHT authorable field types (`AUTHORABLE_TYPES` in the schema dialog), not the twelve `DatasetFieldType` knows — `int64`, `map`, `bytes` and `nil` exist for compatibility and are not offered in the picker. Card 4's join collection is the Data page's 'Add join collection' dialog, which asks for two collections before Create. Its delete clause is the referential-integrity check: `referencedIds` lets one `array-contains` query find every record still pointing at the one being deleted. Card 6's 'refuses a short file' is the export row-count check: the console compares `X-Aglyn-Export-Rows` with the rows received and saves nothing when they differ.

sections.heading: Bind a component and it repeats.
body: Point a component at a dataset in the Besigner and it renders once per record. Filter and sort with the same short expressions the console uses, and a repeat badge tells you when a component is data-driven.

items.title: Repeat
items.body: One component, one record — a list, a grid or a gallery driven by your rows.

items.title: Filter & sort
items.body: Short expressions like status == Open or posted desc — the same syntax the console’s Data page filters and sorts with.

items.title: Limit
items.body: Cap each repeat at the rows a section needs — up to 100 records per repeat.

image.describe: Datasets schema mockup, 880×580 in this section. Topbar breadcrumb '/ Job openings / Schema'. Three tiles — 'Fields in this model' 6 / 'in display order'; 'Sharing' All sites / 'enforced on the server'; 'Records' 48 / 'of 10,000 on Pro'. Below, the model table — Display name, Reference ID, Type, Validation, Required, Description — with the same six fields in the same order as the records shot: Code / code / Text / Pattern / Required / 'Requisition code'; Title / title / Text / 1–120 chars / Required / 'Shown as the listing heading'; Team / team / Reference / → Teams / Required / 'One Teams record'; Headcount / headcount / Integer / min 1 / Optional / 'Hires planned for the role'; Status / status / Text / Open, On hold / Optional / 'Pre-filled as Open'; Posted / posted / Date & time / — / Required / 'Date the role was posted'. Required renders as the house chip, green Required and grey Optional.

sections.notes: The schema shot carries the display-name-versus-reference-id distinction as two adjacent columns, which is the only way to show it without prose, and it is the page's evidence for the per-field description. Every cell is a real model capability: `validation.regex` (Pattern), `min`/`max` as a text length or a number bound, `options` (the schema dialog's comma-separated enum), a single `reference`, and `default` ('Pre-filled when creating documents'). The filter and sort syntax is `parseDatasetFilter`/`parseDatasetSort` in `dataset-query.ts`, which both the Data page's Filter and Sort inputs and a repeat's `repeatFilter`/`repeatSort` use. Limit is `repeatLimit`, capped by `REPEAT_MAX_RECORDS` (100). Today the only repeat marker is the notice in the element props panel ('Repeats over dataset …'); the canvas repeat badge the body names, the copies on the canvas, and Repeat on any component rather than Stack alone arrive with AGL-3111 (see claimsToVerify).

sections.heading: From a model to a live page.

items.title: Model
items.body: Open the Data page in your organization, name the collection, and give each field the type it needs — with a display name, a description, and the rules it should hold.

items.title: Fill
items.body: Type records in the console, import a CSV or JSON file, point a form at the dataset, or POST them to /v1 on Business and up. The console and the API validate every record.

items.title: Publish
items.body: Bind a component to the dataset and publish. A record you write later shows on the live page within seconds.

sections.notes: Step 03 names a refresh window, 'within seconds', that AGL-3113 has to make true: today no record write announces to the live caches, so a changed record shows only after a publish on that site or once the hour-long page cache lapses. The page must not go live before AGL-3113 ships — see claimsToVerify. Step 02 carries the /v1 plan gate: `apiAccess` is false on Starter and Pro, and this page otherwise says datasets start at Starter.

claimsToVerify.phrase: A record you write later shows on the live page within seconds.
claimsToVerify.concern: GATED on AGL-3113: the page must not go live before AGL-3113 ships. Today no record write announces to the live caches. The tenant caches dataset reads for `PUBLISHED_SITE_DATA_TTL_SECONDS` (3600, `render-cache.ts`) and the catch-all page revalidates at 3600, so a changed record shows only after a publish on that site or once the hour lapses. AGL-3113 announces every successful record write (console edits and imports, /v1 `createRecord`/`updateRecord`, the form leg, the dataset steps of Actions and workflows, and site import) to the live pages of every site the dataset is shared with, within about ten seconds. The earlier step 03 named no window and pointed at `POST /v1/sites/{siteId}/publish` (AGL-2462), because the hour-long cache was the only window the code honored. Once AGL-3113 ships, recheck with a signed-out fetch of a page that repeats over the dataset, and read any window from the code, never from a docblock.

claimsToVerify.phrase: let forms, workflows and the API write to the same rows / Forms, workflows and the API / A bound form, a workflow action and the /v1 API write the same rows as the record editor
claimsToVerify.concern: GATED on AGL-3105: the page must not go live before AGL-3105 ships. Today a workflow cannot write a record: each workflow step only calls a host function (`HostWorkflowStep` in `libs/aglyn/src/lib/app-utils/workflows.ts`, run by `run-event-workflows.ts`), and the automation steps that write records are the Actions steps `datasetAppend` and `updateDataset` (`actions.ts`, run by `run-event-actions.ts`). AGL-3105 makes every server-side Actions step type a step of a workflow and reuses the Actions executors, so a workflow writes the same rows through the same step. It keeps the Actions tier gates (server-side steps are Pro and up), which the page does not state; naming that gate stays a copy decision.

claimsToVerify.section: hero (body) + deep-dive (heading, body and Repeat item)
claimsToVerify.phrase: bind them to a component that repeats / Bind a component and it repeats. / Point a component at a dataset in the Besigner and it renders once per record … a repeat badge tells you when a component is data-driven. / One component, one record — a list, a grid or a gallery driven by your rows.
claimsToVerify.concern: GATED on AGL-3111: the page must not go live before AGL-3111 ships. The runtime already expands any node that carries `repeatDataset` (`expandRepeatables`, called from `compose-screen-nodes.ts`); the gap is the editor. Today only the MUI Stack offers Repeat (`libs/plugins/mui/src/lib/components/stack.ts`), the Besigner canvas renders the template once while the copies appear only on the live site, and the only marker is the Attributes panel notice 'Repeats over dataset …' (`element-props-form.component.tsx`). AGL-3111 offers Repeat on every element and component instance, previews the copies on the canvas from the real rows, and adds a repeat badge to the editor overlay. It also settles what repeats (a container repeats its children per record, a leaf element or instance repeats itself), so recheck 'one component, one record' against what ships.

claimsToVerify.phrase: storage past your band meters at the published rate
claimsToVerify.concern: RESOLVED — but note the asymmetry, because it is easy to state backwards. Record count is a HARD band: a write past `recordsPerDataset` is refused at the console route and the /v1 record handler, skipped by the form leg, and refused by the workflow step, and there is no per-record overage. Dataset STORAGE is the opposite: every plan carrying an `extraDataGbMonthlyUsd` rate resolves to 'never-blocks' and bills the overage instead. The copy meters storage and never claims records are metered. Do not merge the two into one sentence.

claimsToVerify.phrase: Text, boolean, integer, number, date and time, coordinates, list and reference / 8 built-in field types
claimsToVerify.concern: RESOLVED. `DatasetFieldType` has twelve members. The schema dialog's picker offers the eight in `AUTHORABLE_TYPES`, then every type a plugin registers (`listCustomFieldTypes()`; Marketplace registers a rating type). `int64`, `map`, `bytes` and `nil` are carried for compatibility and are only shown when an existing field already holds one. The stat counts the built-in eight: 'field types you can author' was false as soon as a plugin adds a type. If `AUTHORABLE_TYPES` gains a type, the card and the stat move together.

claimsToVerify.phrase: validated against on every server-side write — from the console, from a form, from a workflow, or over the API / Four ways in, one set of rules / Every path validates against the same model.
claimsToVerify.concern: RESOLVED by rewriting all four. Only two writers validate: the console dataset route and the /v1 record handlers run `coerceDocumentValues` + `validateDocument`. The form-submission leg (`apps/tenant/app/api/forms/submit/route.ts`) and the `datasetAppend`/`updateDataset` step (`libs/tenant/runtime/src/lib/run-event-actions.ts`) build values with `buildDatasetRecordValues`, which keeps known field ids as strings and checks no type or rule. That step runs as an Actions step today and becomes a workflow step with AGL-3105, which is why the statement notes and card 5 call it a workflow action. The copy now credits validation to the console and the API only, and card 5 claims just the shared rows and the by-id binding. The form leg is also best-effort: with the record or storage quota full, the submission still lands in the Inbox and the row is skipped. The docs page `content-and-data/datasets/overview.md` says the same: console and API records are validated, while form submissions and automation steps store their values as text without validating them.

claimsToVerify.phrase: Typed datasets, shared across your sites. / Shared with the sites you pick / a collection can drive pages on any site it is shared with, and the server enforces that sharing / 2 ways to share: all or selected sites
claimsToVerify.concern: RESOLVED. An organization holds many datasets (`datasetsPerOrg`), and each is shared on its own. The sharing control offers exactly two choices, All sites and Selected sites… (the `org` and `hosts` items in `dataset-schema-dialog.component.tsx`); there is no 'This site only' option. The server enforces the choice: `libs/tenant/runtime/src/lib/get-datasets.ts` checks `visibleToHost` on every dataset it reads for a host, so this is not a console-only affordance. The earlier heading and card title, 'One data store behind every site you run.' and 'One store, every site', framed a single store on every site, which a Selected-sites dataset contradicts. Note the cap the copy does not state: a Selected-sites scope holds at most `MAX_SCOPE_HOSTS` (30) sites, because `array-contains-any` caps there, and the dialog refuses a larger selection rather than widening it. All sites has no cap.

OPEN as a design question, not a truth question. Ten cards on a 3-up grid wrap 3+3+3+1. Every other detail page will reach ten the moment Datasets is added to their Explore grids, so this is the shape the whole set is heading for. Either accept the trailing card — the built /product page already ships a 10-card grid that wraps the same way — or re-cut the grid to a 4-up. Do not resolve it by dropping a product from the roster; that is the failure AGL-2736 and AGL-2759 were both filed for.

claimsToVerify.phrase: Search — Records reachable through a published repeatable are indexed by your site’s search.
claimsToVerify.concern: RESOLVED by cutting it. Site search keeps no index of records: `apps/tenant/utils/search-content.ts` scans at most `DATASET_RECORD_SCAN_LIMIT` (50) records per reachable dataset per query and returns at most 5 rows from each, so a record past the first 50 is never found. Replaced by 'Limit' (`repeatLimit`, capped at `REPEAT_MAX_RECORDS`).

claimsToVerify.phrase: generate a join collection in one click / 1-click many-to-many join collection
claimsToVerify.concern: RESOLVED by cutting 'one click'. 'Add join collection' opens a dialog that asks for a first and a second collection before Create. The card now says 'create a join collection that pairs two', and the stat became '7 filter operators'.

RESOLVED by cutting it. The code names four doors onto records (the console route, /v1, the form leg and the workflow step), but import rides the console route and restoring a site export writes records too, so the figure depends on what a reader counts. Its first replacement, '1 model, on every site that shares it', repeated the single-store framing and gave a reader nothing to act on, so the stat is now '2 ways to share: all or selected sites' (see the sharing entry).

OPEN. True per record up to a bound: the tenant reads at most `REPEAT_MAX_RECORDS` (100) records per dataset and filters and sorts those in memory (`dataset-query.ts`), so on a larger dataset a filter or sort only considers the first 100 rows read. The Limit item states the 100 cap; whether the page should also say that filter and sort are bounded is a copy decision, not a fact to look up.

claimsToVerify.phrase: the API / the /v1 API / POST them to /v1
claimsToVerify.concern: RESOLVED. The API is Business and up (`apiAccess` is false on Starter and Pro) while datasets start at Starter. Step 02 carries the gate, so the page does not imply API access from Starter.

claimsToVerify.phrase: Mockup/Datasets Records and Mockup/Datasets Schema sample data
claimsToVerify.concern: RESOLVED. Both mockups used products — SKU, price, availability, 'Shown on the product card' — which implied a Commerce relationship that does not exist. They now show one Job openings dataset: the same six fields in the same display order, the same record count, and a model whose every cell is a real capability.
